title: What do we get when we add up the hexagonal numbers?
description: The hexagonal numbers one, seven, nineteen and thirty seven are added up one step at a time. The totals are one, eight, twenty seven and sixty four, and a picture of blocks shows each hexagonal number as one layer of the next cube.
teaching_notes: One idea: each hexagonal number is the layer of blocks that turns one cube into the next bigger cube. Watch for students who think the layer is added on one face only.

source: Figure it Out Q8 (Try This), p.9
video_script.why: The child builds running totals of the hexagonal numbers, as in the solved example, and uses a picture of blocks in a cube to explain which sequence comes out.
video_script.substitution: The numbers are the hexagonal numbers instead of three, six, nine and twelve.
video_script.anchor: a small block that grows into bigger cubes, one layer at a time
video_script.payoff_line: Adding up the hexagonal numbers gives the cube numbers
maths_rules: a layer of 7 blocks round three faces of a 1 block cube makes a 2 by 2 by 2 cube, 8 blocks
a layer of 19 blocks makes the 3 by 3 by 3 cube, 27 blocks; a layer of 37 makes 64
video_script.design: One block grows into a bigger cube each time a layer of blocks is wrapped round three of its faces. The running totals sit beside the cubes.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the hexagonal numbers.
<bookmark mark='hex'/>They are one, seven, nineteen, thirty seven and so on.
<bookmark mark='sums'/>We add them up, one, then one plus seven, then one plus seven plus nineteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which sequence do we get? Can a picture of a cube explain it?

beats.on_screen: the numbers and sums stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the hexagonal numbers with a bracket that grows over them, each total written below; a single block beside them

marks.way: the numbers move to the side
marks.grow: a bracket grows over the numbers, one more each time

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='grow'/>The bracket grows by one more number each time, so each total holds every number so far.
<bookmark mark='block'/>Each number can also be a layer of blocks.

marks.given: the hexagonal numbers are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the hexagonal numbers one, seven, nineteen and thirty seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the running totals, and a picture of a cube for them
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the running totals, and explain them with a picture of a cube.

marks.first: the first total is the first number, 1
marks.more: the next number joins the bracket each time, and the totals 8, 27 and 64 are written below

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, add the numbers up one at a time. The first total is one.
<bookmark mark='more'/>One plus seven is eight. One plus seven plus nineteen is twenty seven, and adding thirty seven gives sixty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: picture: 1 block + a layer of 7 blocks = a cube of 8 blocks; + a layer of 19 blocks = a cube of 27 blocks

marks.seven: a layer of seven blocks wraps round three faces of the block and makes a cube of eight blocks
marks.nineteen: a layer of nineteen blocks wraps round three faces and makes a bigger cube of twenty seven blocks

beats.colours: first block in gold, each new layer in a new shade
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, start with one block.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Wrap a layer of seven blocks round three of its faces. It becomes a cube of eight blocks, two by two by two.
<bookmark mark='nineteen'/>Wrap a layer of nineteen blocks round it. It becomes a cube of twenty seven blocks.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check: 3 x 3 = 9, 9 x 3 = 27 blocks; 4 x 4 = 16, 16 x 4 = 64 blocks, the same as the totals

marks.three: a cube three blocks long, wide and tall is counted: nine blocks in a layer, three layers, twenty seven
marks.four: a cube four blocks long, wide and tall is counted: sixteen blocks in a layer, four layers, sixty four

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, check the cubes by counting. A cube three blocks long, wide and tall has nine blocks in a layer. Three layers make twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='four'/>A cube four blocks long, wide and tall has sixteen blocks in a layer. Four layers make sixty four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1, 8, 27, 64, ... the cube numbers; each hexagonal number is one layer of the next cube

marks.ans: the totals are boxed with their name beside the growing cubes

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Adding up the hexagonal numbers gives the cube numbers. Each one is a layer of the next cube.
